name: Dr. Kenji Tanaka
background: Materials scientist with ten years at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory studying microgravity crystallography and vacuum-native fabrication. Holds three patents on processes for growing ultra-pure semiconductor wafers in orbital conditions. Left JPL two years ago to found Orbital Forge with two co-founders: a former SpaceX propulsion engineer and a veteran semiconductor process engineer from TSMC. The team has run two suborbital test flights validating core fabrication parameters. Now seeking Series A funding to build and launch the first orbital manufacturing module.
personality: Quietly intense, speaks with the precision of someone who has spent a decade in a laboratory where imprecision costs missions. Does not oversell but the depth of his knowledge is immediately apparent. Uses specific technical language but can translate when needed. More comfortable with technical questions than market questions. Deeply credible on the science; working to build fluency on the commercial side.
motivation: Has known since his first microgravity experiment that space is a fundamentally better environment for certain manufacturing processes. Spent a decade proving it in the lab. Now believes launch cost reductions have finally made the economics viable and feels a responsibility to move from research to reality before the window closes.

capital.embodied_detail: World-class expertise in microgravity materials science and vacuum-native fabrication. Deep knowledge of orbital mechanics relevant to manufacturing operations. Co-founders bring complementary depth in propulsion engineering and semiconductor process engineering. The team collectively covers the technical surface area of the problem.
capital.objectified_detail: Three granted patents on orbital fabrication processes. Two successful suborbital test flights with validated crystallography data. Partnership with a major semiconductor company (under NDA) willing to purchase output if orbital production targets are met. Detailed mission architecture and financial model built with SpaceX launch cost actuals.
capital.institutional_detail: NASA JPL, three patents, and two co-founders with TSMC and SpaceX on their resumes constitute the strongest possible institutional signal for this domain. These are exactly the credentials that tell a deep-tech investor this team has seen the inside of the problem.
capital.social_detail: Strong network in the aerospace and materials science research community. NASA relationships provide access to facilities and potential government contracts. Co-founders bring semiconductor industry relationships. Limited VC network but warm introductions through JPL alumni and the semiconductor partnership.
capital.symbolic_detail: High symbolic capital with a technically rigorous investor, but with an important ceiling: even Priya's deep-tech expertise does not fully prepare her to evaluate orbital manufacturing economics. Kenji's credentials establish that the science is real. Whether the economics work is a question his track record cannot fully answer -- it has never been done commercially. His symbolic capital buys credibility for the technical claims but cannot resolve the market uncertainty.
